overview: Swarnagiri Sri Venkateswara Swamy Devasthanam, also known as Yadadri Tirumala Devasthanam, is a modern Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Venkateswara Swamy, located atop the scenic Manepally Hills (Swarnagiri Hills) in Anantharam Rural, Bhuvanagiri, Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana — about 47 km from Hyderabad. Built by the Manepally family (Manepally Charitable Trust / Srivari Seva Trust) on 22 acres of their own land, construction began in 2018 and the temple was consecrated on 6 March 2024 by Tridandi Chinna Jeeyar Swamy, following Sri Pancharatra Agama and Tennacharya Sampradaya. The temple features a 12-foot black-granite Venkateswara idol (the largest in Telangana), a 40-foot monolithic Hanuman, a 27-foot Anjaneya, a five-storied Vimana Gopuram, four Rajagopurams, a 1.5-ton bronze bell (India's second-largest), a water-filled Jala Narayana Swamy Sannidhi, multiple sub-shrines (Padmavati, Lakshmi Narasimha, Bhu Varaha, Madan Gopal Krishna, Anjaneya, Ganesha, Vakula Matha, Garuda, Ramanujacharya, Godadevi), and 108 steps leading up to the hilltop. Daily footfall is 70,000–80,000 (crossing 1 lakh on festivals). General darshan is free; special darshan tickets start at ₹50. Open 5 AM to 9 PM daily.
summary: Swarnagiri Sri Venkateswara Swamy Devasthanam, also called Yadadri Tirumala Devasthanam, is a modern Hindu temple in Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana (~47 km from Hyderabad), atop the Manepally Hills. Built by the Manepally family on 22 acres, it was consecrated on 6 March 2024 by Tridandi Chinna Jeeyar Swamy. The temple features a 12-foot Venkateswara idol (the largest in Telangana), a 40-foot monolithic Hanuman, a five-storied Vimana Gopuram, four Rajagopurams, a 1.5-ton bronze bell, a water-filled Jala Narayana Swamy Sannidhi, and 11+ sub-shrines. Daily footfall 70,000–80,000. General darshan is free; special darshan tickets start at ₹50. Open 5 AM – 9 PM daily (5–6:30 AM Bhoopali/Abhishekam; 9 PM Shejarti/closing).

history.content: The idea of building Swarnagiri Temple came from a deeply personal miracle in the Manepally family. In 2016, Vijayalaxmi, the wife of Sri Manepally Rama Rao, had a life-threatening accident in an escalator that broke her bones and pushed her into a coma. The doctors gave up. It was the holy water (tirtham) that somebody brought from Tirupati that brought her back to life. The Manepally family, in thanksgiving, decided to use their own land to build a temple to Lord Venkateswara — to celebrate the miracle and offer a Tirupati-like spiritual hub closer to Hyderabad. The Manepally family is a prominent jewellery business family from Telangana, led by Sri Manepally Rama Rao (a businessman and philanthropist) along with his two sons, trustees Smt Manepally Vijaya Lakshmi, Manepally Murali Krishna, Manepally Sri Latha, Manepally Gopi Krishna, and Manepally Mamatha. Under the Manepally Charitable Trust (also called the Srivari Seva Trust, established 30 January 2024), the family dedicated approximately 22 acres of prime land on a hillock that overlooks the historic Bhongir landscape. The name 'Swarnagiri' (meaning 'Golden Hill') was chosen to reflect the inner radiance and spiritual wealth the temple aims to bestow.
history.foundation_year: Construction began in 2018; temple formally consecrated (Prana Pratishtha + Kumbhabhishekam) on 6 March 2024 by Tridandi Sri Sri Sri Chinna Jeeyar Swamy (per the Telugu Wikipedia; some English sources say 7 March 2024 — both dates are close and refer to the consecration festivities).

legends: In 2016, Smt Manepally Vijaya Lakshmi had a life-threatening escalator accident, broke her bones, and was pushed into a coma. Doctors gave up, but tirtham (holy water) brought from Tirupati brought her back to life.
The Manepally family then decided to use their own land to build a temple to Lord Venkateswara as a way of thanksgiving and to celebrate the miracle.
Construction began in 2018, and after over six years of work, the temple was consecrated on 6 March 2024 by Tridandi Chinna Jeeyar Swamy.

The temple was designed to follow the Sri Pancharatra Agama and Tennacharya Sampradaya traditions, with each ritual — from the foundation stone to the final installation of the deity — adhering to ancient Agama Shastra traditions.
The temple is named 'Swarnagiri' (Golden Hill) to reflect the inner radiance and spiritual wealth it aims to bestow upon visitors.

sthala_puranam: Swarnagiri Temple does not have a traditional ancient Sthala Puranam because it is a modern temple — built between 2018 and 2024 and consecrated only in 2024. The site's sacred character is derived from: (1) The Manepally family's personal miracle in 2016 (recovery of Smt Manepally Vijaya Lakshmi from a coma after tirtham from Tirupati), which inspired the temple construction; (2) The temple's dedication to Lord Venkateswara Swamy, whose main idol is a 12-foot black-granite statue (the largest Venkateswara idol in Telangana); (3) The Prana Pratishtha and Kumbhabhishekam performed by Tridandi Chinna Jeeyar Swamy in March 2024 — which infuses the hilltop with divine energy and authentic Sri Vaishnava Agama sanctity; (4) The 108 steps symbolising the spiritual climb to the sanctum; (5) The 1.5-ton bronze bell (India's second largest temple bell); and (6) The hilltop location (Manepally / Swarnagiri Hills) overlooking the historic Bhongir landscape — chosen for its picturesque setting that enhances the spiritual experience.
religious_significance: Swarnagiri is significant in five ways: (1) It houses the largest Venkateswara idol in Telangana (12 feet tall, in black granite, gold- and silver-adorned); (2) It is consecrated by Tridandi Chinna Jeeyar Swamy — one of the most revered Sri Vaishnava Acharyas — so every ritual follows authentic Pancharatra Agama and Tennacharya Sampradaya; (3) It is widely considered a 'Tirupati of Telangana' — offering Tirumala-like darshan within 50 km of Hyderabad for devotees who cannot travel to Andhra Pradesh frequently; (4) It draws 70,000–80,000 devotees daily (crossing 1 lakh on festivals) and is rapidly becoming one of the most-visited pilgrimage sites in Telangana; (5) It is part of the larger Yadadri temple circuit, along with Yadadri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple and Bhongir Fort.
spiritual_significance: Devotees believe that praying to Lord Venkateswara at Swarnagiri brings financial stability, career success, and fulfilment of wishes. The 12-foot black-granite idol is considered especially powerful because of the Agama Shastra rituals performed at consecration and the daily pancha-samskara rituals. The illuminated Jala Narayana Swamy Sannidhi (water-filled sanctum) is a unique feature that gives visitors a meditative experience in the evening. The 40-foot monolithic Hanuman is venerated for protection, courage, and removal of obstacles. The 108 steps symbolise the spiritual ascent to the divine. The 1.5-ton bronze bell is rung during aarti and is said to carry prayers to the divine. Many devotees also visit Swarnagiri as part of the Yadadri temple circuit (Yadadri + Swarnagiri + Bhongir Fort + Kolanupaka Jain Temple) for a half-day spiritual trip from Hyderabad.
healing_beliefs: Lord Venkateswara worship — financial stability, career success, fulfilment of wishes (per multiple devotional sources)
Panchamukha Hanuman (40-foot monolithic statue) — protection from evil, black magic, evil eye, and negative energies; courage and strength
Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy — protection and relief from fear; devotion to Narasimha removes all obstacles
Jala Narayana Swamy — meditative and calming experience; the water-filled sanctum is said to represent the cosmic ocean
Madan Gopal Krishna — child blessings and family wellbeing
Bhu Varaha Swamy — earth, stability, and agricultural prosperity
miracles_and_devotee_experiences: The temple's existence is itself tied to a miracle: In 2016, Smt Manepally Vijaya Lakshmi recovered from a life-threatening escalator accident and coma after tirtham from Tirupati was brought to her; doctors had given up.
Devotees report life-changing experiences at the 40-foot monolithic Hanuman statue — believed to be one of the most powerful protective Hanuman murtis in Telangana.
The Jala Narayana Swamy Sannidhi is reported as 'a visual spectacle to visitors in the evenings' (per Deccan Chronicle) — the illuminated water-filled sanctum creates a unique meditative atmosphere.
Daily footfall of 70,000–80,000 devotees (crossing 1 lakh on festivals) is a testament to the temple's growing spiritual pull (per Deccan Chronicle interview with Sri Manepally Rama Rao).
The 1.5-ton bronze bell, said to be India's second-largest temple bell, is rung during aarti and is a popular photo/video subject on social media.
architecture: Swarnagiri Temple is a modern masterpiece of Dravidian architecture, drawing inspiration from the Pallava, Chola, Chalukya, and Vijayanagara styles. The temple complex is spread across 22 acres atop the Manepally Hills. The architecture features: (1) Four majestic Rajagopurams (temple gateways) on four sides of the prakara (outer wall), each adorned with intricate carvings and sacred patterns; (2) A five-storied Vimana Gopuram rising above the sanctum sanctorum (Garbha Griha); (3) The Garbha Griha houses a 12-foot-tall black-granite idol of Lord Venkateswara Swamy (the largest Venkateswara idol in Telangana) — flanked by Goddesses Sridevi and Bhu Devi; (4) A 40-foot monolithic Hanuman statue (with a 27-foot Anjaneya as per the Telugu Wikipedia) and a massive 1.5-ton bronze bell (India's second-largest); (5) A spacious pradakshina path and well-planned mandapams (Maha Mandapam, Kalyana Mandapam, Yagasala); (6) The Jala Narayana Swamy Sannidhi — an illuminated water-filled sanctum that is a visual highlight in the evenings; (7) Sub-shrines of Padmavati, Lakshmi Narasimha, Bhu Varaha, Madan Gopal Krishna, Anjaneya, Ganesha, Vakula Matha, Garuda, Ramanujacharya, Godadevi; (8) A 40-foot tall Ratham (chariot) per the Telugu Wikipedia; (9) 108 steps leading from the foothills to the temple complex; (10) A Garuda Sthambham and a Pushkarini (sacred tank) with Vedic scholars' idols.
architectural_style: Modern Dravidian (Pallava + Chola + Chalukya + Vijayanagara inspired); Pancharatra Agama; Tennacharya Sampradaya; 22 acres; 108 steps to the hilltop; 12-foot black-granite Venkateswara idol; 40-foot monolithic Hanuman; 5-storied Vimana Gopuram; 4 Rajagopurams; 1.5-ton bronze bell

darshan_and_tickets.general_darshan: Free for all devotees. Timings: 5:00 AM – 9:00 PM daily (with break 12:30 PM – 1:30 PM). Free Mahaprasad is distributed from 1:30 PM – 2:30 PM (per hyderabadtourism.travel).
darshan_and_tickets.special_darshan: Seegra Darshanam: ₹50 per person; Srivari Donor Darshan: ₹300 per person; Seva Darshan: ₹500 per person. Online booking available via swarnagiritemple.com / ytdtemple.com / tickets99.com.
darshan_and_tickets.ticket_details: Free general darshan. Seegra Darshanam ₹50. Srivari Donor Darshan ₹300. Special sevas range from ₹100 (Archana) to ₹51,000 (Vishesha Kalyanam). Poolangi Seva (Tue/Thu/Sat): ₹21,000. Srivari Nitya Kalyanam: ₹2,001. Sahasra Nama Archana: ₹1,100. Vedha Ashirvachanam: ₹2,501. Tickets can be booked online at swarnagiritemple.com, ytdtemple.com, or via tickets99.com. Prasadam items (Laddu, Vada, Pulihora, Tulabaram items) can be purchased online. Photography is restricted inside the temple premises.

dress_code: Swarnagiri Temple follows a simple and traditional dress code that aligns with Vaishnava temple customs. Men: dhoti-kurta, pancha or formal pants paired with a shirt are appropriate. Women: saree, salwar kameez, churidar, or long skirt with dupatta. Traditional attire is especially recommended during special sevas or festive occasions. Maintain proper dress and decorum to preserve the sanctity of the temple. Avoid shorts, sleeveless tops, mini skirts, ripped jeans, or any revealing outfits inside the temple premises.

accommodation.availability: On-site temple accommodation is available at Swarnagiri Sree Venkateswara Swami Devasthanam — including AC rooms with 2, 4, and 6 beds, a 2 BHK cottage, and a Dormitory Hall (per yatradham.org). Meals and parking facilities are available for all guests. Off-site options are also available in Bhuvanagiri town (~10 km), Bhongir, Yadadri, and Hyderabad.

best_time_to_visit: October to March is the most pleasant weather window. Special days: Brahmotsavam (10 days in March/April — the most important festival), Vaikunta Ekadashi (Dec/Jan), Hanuman Jayanti (March/April), Sri Rama Navami, Sri Krishna Janmashtami. For the most comfortable experience, visit on a weekday morning (5:00–8:00 AM) or in the evening (4:00–8:00 PM). The illuminated Jala Narayana Swamy Sannidhi is best viewed in the evening. Most visitors combine Swarnagiri with Yadadri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple (~18 km), Bhongir Fort (~10 km), Surendrapuri (~20 km), and Kolanupaka Jain Temple (~35 km) for a full-day pilgrimage circuit from Hyderabad.

travel.road: Located on the Manepally Hills near Bhuvanagiri, ~47 km from Hyderabad (1.5–2 hours drive). Take NH 163 (Uppal → Ghatkesar → Bhongir → Swarnagiri) or the ORR Warangal NH 163 via the Ghatkesar exit. TGSRTC operates special buses from MGBS (Mahatma Gandhi Bus Stand) and JBS (Jubilee Bus Stand) to Yadadri, with onward connection to Swarnagiri. Buses from Hyderabad MGBS to Yadadri: 57 km; from JBS to Yadadri: 55.8 km (per official bus table). Private buses also run.
travel.rail: Nearest railway station is Bhongir (Bhuvanagiri) Railway Station — ~10 km. Yadadri Railway Station — ~18 km. Direct trains from Secunderabad to Yadadri: Krishna Express (17406, 06:00 → 06:48, daily); SC-WL (746, 09:35 → 10:19, daily); SC BDCR EXP (17659, 17:25 → 18:29, daily); HYB KZJ SPL (7758, 19:10 → 20:09, daily).
travel.air: Nearest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad — ~50 km / ~71 km per different sources (1.5–2 hours drive).
travel.nearest_railway_station: Bhongir (Bhuvanagiri) Railway Station (~10 km); Yadadri Railway Station (~18 km)
travel.nearest_bus_station: Bhuvanagiri Bus Stand (~10 km); Yadadri Bus Terminal (~18 km); direct TGSRTC services from Hyderabad MGBS and JBS
travel.nearest_airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~50–71 km)

travel_tips: Plan to spend at least half a day to fully explore Swarnagiri — the temple is sprawling with many sub-shrines.
Wear comfortable footwear (which you'll remove at temple entrances) and be prepared to climb 108 steps (lifts available for senior citizens and disabled visitors).
Visit during early morning (5:00–8:00 AM) or evening (4:00–8:00 PM) for a peaceful darshan and to see the illuminated Jala Narayana Swamy Sannidhi.
Carry minimal belongings for quicker security checks; cameras and mobile phones are not allowed inside the temple.

introduction.en: Swarnagiri Sri Venkateswara Swamy Devasthanam, also known as Yadadri Tirumala Devasthanam, is a modern Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Venkateswara Swamy, located atop the scenic Manepally Hills in Anantharam Rural, Bhuvanagiri, Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana — about 47 km from Hyderabad. Built by the Manepally family (Manepally Charitable Trust / Srivari Seva Trust) on 22 acres of their own land, construction began in 2018 and the temple was consecrated on 6 March 2024 by Tridandi Chinna Jeeyar Swamy, following Sri Pancharatra Agama and Tennacharya Sampradaya. The temple features a 12-foot black-granite Venkateswara idol (the largest in Telangana), a 40-foot monolithic Hanuman, a five-storied Vimana Gopuram, four Rajagopurams, a 1.5-ton bronze bell (India's second-largest), and a water-filled Jala Narayana Swamy Sannidhi. Daily footfall is 70,000–80,000. Open 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily. General darshan is free; special darshan tickets start at ₹50.

history.en: The idea of building Swarnagiri Temple came from a deeply personal miracle in the Manepally family. In 2016, Vijayalaxmi, the wife of Sri Manepally Rama Rao, had a life-threatening escalator accident that broke her bones and pushed her into a coma. Doctors gave up, but tirtham (holy water) brought from Tirupati brought her back to life. The family, in thanksgiving, decided to use their own land to build a temple to Lord Venkateswara. Construction began in 2018, and after over six years of work, the temple was consecrated on 6 March 2024 by Tridandi Chinna Jeeyar Swamy. The name 'Swarnagiri' (meaning 'Golden Hill') was chosen to reflect the inner radiance and spiritual wealth the temple aims to bestow. The Manepally Charitable Trust (also called the Srivari Seva Trust, established 30 January 2024) manages the temple. The trust is led by Sri Manepally Rama Rao and his family (Smt Manepally Vijaya Lakshmi, Manepally Murali Krishna, Manepally Sri Latha, Manepally Gopi Krishna, and Manepally Mamatha).

travel_guide.en: Swarnagiri is on the Manepally Hills near Bhuvanagiri, ~47 km from Hyderabad (1.5–2 hours drive). Take NH 163 (Uppal → Ghatkesar → Bhongir → Swarnagiri) or the ORR Warangal NH 163 via the Ghatkesar exit. TGSRTC operates special buses from MGBS and JBS to Yadadri (57 km and 55.8 km respectively), with onward connection to Swarnagiri. The nearest railway station is Bhongir (~10 km) or Yadadri (~18 km). Direct trains from Secunderabad to Yadadri: Krishna Express (17406), SC-WL (746), SC BDCR EXP (17659), HYB KZJ SPL (7758). The nearest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~50–71 km). Open 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily (with break 12:30 PM – 1:30 PM). Free Mahaprasad distributed 1:30 PM – 2:30 PM. On-site temple accommodation starts at ₹789/night. Combine with Yadadri (~18 km), Bhongir Fort (~10 km), Surendrapuri (~20 km), and Kolanupaka Jain Temple (~35 km) for a full-day pilgrimage circuit.

faq.answer: Swarnagiri is a modern Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Venkateswara Swamy, located atop the scenic Manepally Hills in Anantharam Rural, Bhuvanagiri, Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana — about 47 km from Hyderabad. The temple features a 12-foot black-granite Venkateswara idol (the largest in Telangana), a 40-foot monolithic Hanuman, a five-storied Vimana Gopuram, four Rajagopurams, a 1.5-ton bronze bell (India's second-largest), and a water-filled Jala Narayana Swamy Sannidhi.

faq.question: Where is Swarnagiri Temple located?
faq.answer: Swarnagiri is on the Manepally Hills (Swarnagiri Hills) in Anantharam Rural, Bhuvanagiri, Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana – 508116, India. It is ~47 km from Hyderabad (1.5–2 hours drive), ~10 km from Bhuvanagiri town, ~15–18 km from Yadadri / Yadagirigutta, ~20 km from Surendrapuri, and ~35 km from Kolanupaka Jain Temple. The nearest railway station is Bhongir (~10 km) or Yadadri (~18 km). The nearest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~50–71 km).

faq.question: What are the entry fee and temple timings?
faq.answer: General darshan is FREE for all devotees. Special darshan tickets: Seegra Darshanam ₹50, Srivari Donor Darshan ₹300. Sevas range from ₹100 (Archana) to ₹51,000 (Vishesha Kalyanam). Open 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily. Morning schedule: 5:00 AM Opening, 5:00–6:30 AM Bhoopali and Abhishekam, 6:30 AM – 12:30 PM General Darshan, 12:30 PM – 1:30 PM Lunch Break, 1:30 PM – 2:30 PM Mahaprasad Distribution, 1:30 PM – 8:30 PM General Darshan (afternoon/evening), 8:30 PM – 9:00 PM Ekantha Seva, 9:00 PM Shejarti / temple closes.

faq.question: Who founded Swarnagiri Temple?
faq.answer: Swarnagiri was built by the Manepally family, led by Sri Manepally Rama Rao (a prominent businessman and philanthropist) along with his two sons, trustees Smt Manepally Vijaya Lakshmi, Manepally Murali Krishna, Manepally Sri Latha, Manepally Gopi Krishna, and Manepally Mamatha. The temple was constructed under the Manepally Charitable Trust (also called the Srivari Seva Trust, established 30 January 2024). The idea of building the temple came from a deeply personal miracle in 2016, when Smt Manepally Vijaya Lakshmi recovered from a life-threatening escalator accident and coma after tirtham (holy water) from Tirupati was brought to her. The family, in thanksgiving, decided to use their own land to build a temple to Lord Venkateswara. Construction began in 2018, and the temple was consecrated on 6 March 2024 by Tridandi Chinna Jeeyar Swamy.

faq.question: What is the architecture of Swarnagiri Temple?
faq.answer: Swarnagiri is a modern masterpiece of Dravidian architecture, drawing inspiration from the Pallava, Chola, Chalukya, and Vijayanagara styles. The temple complex is spread across 22 acres atop the Manepally Hills. Key architectural features include: (1) Four majestic Rajagopurams (temple gateways) on four sides of the prakara; (2) A five-storied Vimana Gopuram rising above the Garbha Griha; (3) The Garbha Griha houses a 12-foot black-granite idol of Lord Venkateswara (the largest in Telangana), flanked by Sridevi and Bhu Devi; (4) A 40-foot monolithic Hanuman statue; (5) A 1.5-ton bronze bell (India's second-largest); (6) A water-filled Jala Narayana Swamy Sannidhi (illuminated visual highlight in evenings); (7) Sub-shrines of Padmavati, Lakshmi Narasimha, Bhu Varaha, Madan Gopal Krishna, Anjaneya, Ganesha, Vakula Matha, Garuda, Ramanujacharya, Godadevi; (8) 108 steps leading up to the temple complex; (9) A 40-foot Ratham (chariot); and (10) A Pushkarini (sacred tank) with Vedic scholars' (Veda Murthis) idols.

faq.question: What are the most important festivals at Swarnagiri?
faq.answer: The most important festival is Brahmotsavam — a 10-day grand celebration held annually between March and April (similar to the Tirumala Brahmotsavam). Other major festivals include Vaikunta Ekadashi (Dec/Jan), Rathasapthami, Sri Rama Navami, Sri Krishna Janmashtami, Hanuman Jayanti (March/April), Deepavali, and Vinayaka Chavithi (Ganesh Chaturthi) with Navaratri celebrations. During festivals, darshan timings are extended, special sevas are performed, and footfall exceeds 1 lakh.

faq.question: How much time do I need at Swarnagiri?
faq.answer: Plan to spend at least half a day to fully explore Swarnagiri. The temple has a sprawling 22-acre complex with multiple sub-shrines. Most visitors combine Swarnagiri with Yadadri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple (~15–18 km), Bhongir Fort (~10 km), Surendrapuri (~20 km), and Kolanupaka Jain Temple (~35 km) for a full-day pilgrimage circuit from Hyderabad.

faq.question: Is there accommodation available at Swarnagiri?
faq.answer: Yes — on-site temple accommodation is available at Swarnagiri Sree Venkateswara Swami Devasthanam, including AC rooms with 2, 4, and 6 beds, a 2 BHK cottage, and a Dormitory Hall. Meals and parking facilities are available for all guests. Prices start at ₹789/night (per yatradham.org). Off-site options are also available in Bhuvanagiri town (~10 km), Bhongir (~13 km), Yadadri (~18 km), and Hyderabad (~47 km).

faq.question: How do I reach Swarnagiri Temple from Hyderabad?
faq.answer: By road: ~47 km from Hyderabad (1.5–2 hours drive). Take NH 163 (Uppal → Ghatkesar → Bhongir → Swarnagiri) or the ORR Warangal NH 163 via the Ghatkesar exit. By bus: TGSRTC operates special buses from MGBS (Mahatma Gandhi Bus Stand) and JBS (Jubilee Bus Stand) to Yadadri (57 km and 55.8 km respectively), with onward connection to Swarnagiri. By train: nearest railway station is Bhongir (~10 km) or Yadadri (~18 km). Direct trains from Secunderabad to Yadadri: Krishna Express (17406), SC-WL (746), SC BDCR EXP (17659), HYB KZJ SPL (7758). By air: nearest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~50–71 km).

faq.question: What are the special sevas and their costs?
faq.answer: Swarnagiri offers 24 documented sevas. Daily sevas include: Dakshina Q Entry / Seegra Darshanam (₹50), Archana (₹100), Kumkuma Archana (₹300), Suprabhatha Seva (₹500), Thiruveedhi Utsavam (₹500), Ekantha Seva (₹500), Sahasra Deepaalankarana (₹500), Suvarna Pushparchana (₹900), Vishesha Kumkuma Archana (₹1,000), Sahasra Nama Archana (₹1,100), Vedha Ashirvachanam (₹2,501), Garuda Vahana Seva Pournami (₹2,000), Srivari Nitya Kalyanam (₹2,001), Vishesha Kalyanam (₹51,000). Weekly 3-day: Thomala Seva (₹1,500), Poolangi Seva (₹21,000, Tue/Thu/Sat). Weekly: Ganesh Abhishekam (₹500), Vasavi Matha Abhishekam (₹500), Anjaneya Swamy Abhishekam (₹1,000), Thirupavadi Seva (₹1,500), Vasantotsava Seva (₹2,500). Tickets can be booked online at swarnagiritemple.com, ytdtemple.com, or via tickets99.com.

faq.question: What is the dress code at Swarnagiri Temple?
faq.answer: Swarnagiri Temple follows a simple and traditional dress code that aligns with Vaishnava temple customs. For men: dhoti-kurta, pancha, or formal pants paired with a shirt are appropriate. For women: saree, salwar kameez, churidar, or long skirt with dupatta. Traditional attire is especially recommended during special sevas or festive occasions. Avoid shorts, sleeveless tops, mini skirts, ripped jeans, or any revealing outfits inside the temple premises. Maintain proper dress and decorum to preserve the sanctity of the temple.

faq.question: Is Swarnagiri Temple accessible for elderly and disabled visitors?
faq.answer: Yes — Swarnagiri is wheelchair-accessible at the entrance and exit (per JustDial). Lifts are available for senior citizens and those unable to climb the 108 steps (per bloggymaster.com). Free Mahaprasad is distributed from 1:30 PM – 2:30 PM daily. There is ample parking at the foot of the hill. Photography is restricted inside the temple (cameras and mobile phones not allowed). Switch off your mobile phones at the temples; don't carry weapons or head gear (helmets, caps, turbans) inside the temple premises. Smoking and alcohol consumption are prohibited.
